title: Sigil and Wolf
premise: Marguerite Blackwood keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things through a gate that must never open fully — and she alone can feel its hunger. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, Marguerite and a wolf-marked smuggler named Corren Ash are branded traitors and forced to flee with the guild's most dangerous secret: proof that their country was erased from existence decades ago and rewritten by the throne. Hunted across a land whose borders literally forget them, they seek the true door out while the guild's masters, the crown's witchfinder, and the gate itself all close in. In the end, Marguerite chooses to unmake her own name from the ledger, sealing the gate at the cost of being forgotten by everyone she saved — except Corren, who carries her sigil in his memory.
about_author: Casper Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing documents no one was meant to read, an experience that seeps into every ledger-bound world they write. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and reliable wolves.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She balances the guild's accounts of traded impossibilities — bottled storms, borrowed years — while feeling the sealed gate pulse beneath the counting house. A routine entry goes wrong when ink moves on its own. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath meticulous order; she loves her work but senses it watching her back.

chapters.title: A Wolf at the Counting House
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Corren Ash arrives to sell a stolen relic: a sigil-stone bearing a wolf mark identical to one burned into Marguerite's childhood memory. Their negotiation crackles with mutual suspicion. Emotional beat: recognition without trust; two people who recognize something feral in each other.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Criers announce the Gifted Purge: anyone with magic will be taken for 'examination.' The guild masters calmly begin destroying evidence — including, Marguerite realizes, evidence of people. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal; the machinery she served turns on her kind overnight.

chapters.title: What the Masters Burn
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Ordered to burn ledgers, she secretly copies pages revealing the country's true name has been struck from every record since 'the Correction' forty years ago. The witchfinder Seraphine Vale arrives early. Emotional beat: the first conscious act of treason, thrilling and terrifying.

chapters.title: Seraphine Vale Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. The witchfinder interviews the guild staff with unsettling gentleness, reading truths off skin like braille. Corren hides his wolf-sigil brand under a false story; Marguerite nearly breaks. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse terror where politeness is the weapon.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Forgotten Quarter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. An informant betrays them; Vale raids the counting house. Marguerite and Corren escape through streets that literally blur behind them — the erased country asserting itself. Emotional beat: adrenaline-fueled partnership forged in flight; reluctant reliance becomes real.

chapters.title: The Map That Eats Itself
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Hiding in a smugglers' den, they study her copied pages: roads vanish on maps drawn after the Correction. To leave the country, they need the original door — the gate itself, or what it was before. Emotional beat: despair curdling into purpose; the problem gains shape.

chapters.title: Wolves of the Borderlands
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. He leads her to his old pack — gifted outlaws living in the border fog where the erasure is thinnest. Their leader recognizes Marguerite's sigil and calls her by a name she doesn't know. Emotional beat: belonging offered by strangers; identity shaken loose.

chapters.title: The Name I Don't Remember
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The pack reveals she was born beyond the erased border; her family crossed during the Correction and paid the toll of forgetting. Her gate-keeping gift is a scar from that crossing. Emotional beat: grief for a self she never got to keep.

chapters.title: Vale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV (first time). Vale offers Corren amnesty for Marguerite's capture, revealing the crown hunts the gifted to feed the gate and keep the Correction stable. Corren refuses — but doesn't tell Marguerite. Emotional beat: the antagonist humanized; loyalty complicated by concealment.

chapters.title: Raid on the Fog Camp
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Crown soldiers strike the camp using information only Vale could have — or Corren's meeting leaked another way. The pack scatters; the elder dies passing Marguerite the full truth of the door. Emotional beat: loss, suspicion, and the cost of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: Accusation
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She confronts Corren about his meeting with Vale; he admits the offer but swears he refused. Trust fractures precisely when they need each other most. Emotional beat: heartbreak as suspense; the relationship's lowest point.

chapters.title: The Guild's True Business
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Captured by surviving guild masters, Corren learns the guild didn't trade impossibilities — it manufactured the Correction, and Marguerite's gate is its lock. They want her back as keeper, forever. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything; the enemy is the institution she loved.

chapters.title: Alone in the Erased Country
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Believing Corren sold her out, she travels alone toward the capital gate, watching villages dissolve into fog as the Correction accelerates. Emotional beat: isolation and resolve; she stops running and starts choosing.

chapters.title: The Witchfinder's Confession
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Vale captures Marguerite but confesses she was corrected too — her memories are crown-issue, her cruelty programmed. She wants the gate opened as much as Marguerite does, for different reasons. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance with an enemy; moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Corren Breaks His Cage
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. He escapes the guild, unleashing his suppressed wolf-gift fully for the first time, and races to the capital carrying the ledger page that proves how to unseal the door. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into devotion; the chase begins.

chapters.title: Beneath the Counting House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. All parties converge on the gate chamber: Marguerite and Vale descending, Corren breaking in, guild masters performing the rite to bind Marguerite permanently. Emotional beat: collision course; every debt comes due in one room.

chapters.title: The Gate Opens
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The guild forces the gate wide; the raw erased country pours through — memories, names, the dead demanding restoration. Vale turns against the guild mid-rite. Emotional beat: overwhelming climax of wonder and horror; power revealed as appetite.

chapters.title: Sigil and Wolf
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corren reaches Marguerite inside the gate's maw; together they realize the door out was never geographic — it requires a name freely given to the ledger. The guild masters are consumed by what they built. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen together; love as the counter-spell to corruption.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She writes her own name into the ledger and strikes it, sealing the gate and restoring the country's true name — at the cost of everyone forgetting her. Vale survives, freed, and chooses to remember nothing rather than grieve. Emotional beat: bittersweet climax resolution; erasure transformed from wound to gift.

chapters.title: The Country That Remembers
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. The restored land wakes; borders hold; the gifted are simply people again. Corren walks out of the fog carrying a sigil-stone and a name no one else knows. Emotional beat: mourning woven into hope; the world is healed but incomplete.

chapters.title: Someone to Carry It
chapters.summary: Final chapter, dual POV converging. Months later, Corren finds Marguerite living quietly under no name at all — except he remembers, because she gave him her sigil to hold. They begin again, strangers with a shared history. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt from scratch; identity as something we hand to those who choose to keep it.
